newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended higher across the board in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Friday.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today following a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were quietly steady. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.70/98.75 compared with Thursday's close of S$98.63/98.68, September 2001 at S$97.35/97.40 against 97.30/97.35 and June 2003 at S$95.38/95.43 from S$95.28/95.33.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent versus Thursday's 3-3/4 3-5/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from Thursday's yield of 1.40/1.35 percent and one-year unchanged at 1.85/1.80 percent.
